The fix is OPT-IN: it gives callers a cancellation mechanism but changes nothing unless a signal is passed, so existing cascades are not fixed by this change alone.
fix: Isolated the launch-boom regression half to a temp OPENCLINXR_LOCK_ROOT so fake-browser unit tests never contend for the production slot.

createSlottedChromium launch() accepts opt-in {signal}: AbortSignal in the leading options object, forwarded to withComputeSlot meta and stripped before delegating to playwright (no behavior change without a signal).
Abort while queued rejects promptly without invoking the underlying launch and removes the queue ticket.
Abort after acquire but mid-launch closes the just-launched browser and throws the abort reason.
awaitSlotFree polling (incl. pre-existing first test) because slot-file cleanup settles after the launch promise; instant assertion raced cleanup under load.
defect.priorBehavior: launch() waited on the single browser-capture file-lock slot with no cancellation path (withComputeSlot supports AbortSignal; slotted-playwright never plumbed one). The unit test's launch-boom half used the shared default lock root, so under contention it queued and died at 5s.
defect.rootCause: Demonstrated mechanism (not mere structure): fake-browser unit assertions contended for the real production slot via the default lock root, and slot acquisition was uncancellable. Historical-CI attribution stays provisional pending run-seven.py reruns.
